historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly retains the exact injector/read sequence and requires qualified platform mapping and complete FTrace/register evidence.

historical_reviews.v3_1: Prove a three-stage state transition: clean target registers, latent injected CE with no premature consumption, then the explicit demand read followed by the expected correctable mc0/ch0 shadow, retry log, serial and FTrace `extlog_mem_event`; restore all temporary BIOS/GRUB/DFX settings.

original_test_intent: Demonstrate that a correctable memory error planted without immediate consumption is consumed by a demand read on the intended Intel GNR DIMM and reported through the expected firmware-first machine-check, retry-read and FTrace ELog path.
original_method: Record immutable platform and DIMM topology, harness version and BIOS/GRUB baseline; apply/verify the exact source enablement matrix and DDR5 ECS; map address0x10000 plus mc0/ch0/retry index1 to the intended DIMM; preserve evidence and establish the approved clean register prestate; halt, reset injector lock and issue one CE with `immConsume=False`; capture proof that injection did not already consume; execute `mem(0x10000)` once; capture the named MC shadow and retry entry, resume, collect serial/FTrace extlog/OS/SEL evidence, verify health and restore settings under the recovery plan.
manual_activity: The Intel-qualified owner/FAE validates the BIOS/harness/address mapping and controls halt, injection, demand read, go and recovery; the agent may correlate the approved stage-specific registers and logs.
required_inputs: GNR CPU stepping, BIOS/BMC/OS, DIMM PN/serial/slot and socket/IMC/channel topology
Intel CScripts/error-injection package version/hash/license and exact `immConsume=False`/`mem()` semantics
Project mapping/restoration for every source BIOS/DFX/ELog/WHEA/firmware-first/GRUB knob
Address0x10000 to physical target mapping and mc0.ch0 retry_rd_err_log[1] ownership
Expected clean prestate, correctable MC shadow/MSCOD, retry entry and FTrace extlog_mem_event fields/timing
Dedicated window, serial/OOB path, halt/read/go timeouts, wrong-severity/crash recovery and no-retry plan
safety_requirements: Use a dedicated workload-free SUT with stable power, serial and independent OOB recovery
Preserve general dmesg/journal/SEL/FTrace evidence and BIOS/GRUB baseline; do not perform blanket log clearing
Clear only approved target MC/retry state after capture, and prove the correct target/index
Do not assume 0x10000 is a safe or intended memory location; require vendor harness mapping
Verify the error remains latent after injection and stop if it is consumed early or appears on the wrong channel
Stop on fatal/uncorrectable severity, unexpected MCA, hang, crash or missing response; never automatically reinject or reboot
After evidence capture restore all lock/DFX/error-injection/GRUB settings and verify memory/OS/BMC health
agent_execution_scope: Validate platform, harness, settings, target/index mapping and stage-specific expected evidence
Observe one approved latent injection and demand read while capturing complete CScripts/serial/FTrace/register outputs
Compare restoration and final health to baseline
Do not select address/DIMM, change BIOS/GRUB, clear general logs, substitute Patrol Scrub, retry or decide PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve harness, BIOS mapping and address/register target
Define the latent pre-read proof and post-read MC/retry/extlog oracle
Approve halt/read/go, stop and crash recovery boundaries
Review complete transition/restoration evidence and issue verdict

review_improvement: Restores the source's defining latent injection and explicit demand read, replaces generic log tails with stage-specific register/FTrace proof and adds topology, recovery and settings-restoration control.
independent_technical_reasoning: Demand Scrub coverage depends on causality: the CE is planted without consumption and only the explicit memory access should trigger correction/reporting. If evidence appears before `mem(0x10000)`, the test followed a different path. Conversely, generic corrected logs after the read do not identify mc0/ch0 retry index1 or firmware ELog handling. Exact address-to-DIMM mapping and stage timestamps are therefore decisive, and debug/security changes must be restored independently of whether the CE remained correctable.
